page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with no margin notes. Running head at top centre (Hebrew). Page number 414 at top right. Continuation lines from the previous entry at the top, then dictionary entries, ending with the catchword "Attenua-" at lower right.

main_text.p: להמטיר pluviam demittendo, Job.38.26. מהמטיר Ne pluviam demittant, Jesa.5.6. Futur. אַמְטִיר pluviam demittam, Amos 4.7.

מִי Quis, Qui, Quae: Interrogativum personae propriae, utriusq; generi & numero servientis, sed latius etiam usurpatur. Vide Thesaurum nostrum Grammaticum lib. 2. cap.6. Reg.3. מִי אַתָּה Quis es tu? Genes.27.32. מִי אֵת Quae es tu? Ruth.3.9. מִי אֵלֶּה Qui sunt isti? Gen.33.5. מִי שְׁמֶךָ Quis (es de) nomine tuo, seu, Quod est nomen tuum? Jud.13.v.17. לְמִי אַתָּה Cujus es tu? לְמִי אֵלֶּה Cujus sunt ista? Genes.32.18. Hinc בִּשְׁלַמִּי Cujus causā, Propter quem? Jonae 1.7. ex ב & מִי & שֶׁל compositum.

מַיִם m. Aqua, Aquae: Forma numeri dualis videtur duplicem aquam notare, de qua Gen.1.6.7. Jungitur quoque Verbo singularis numeri, ut Genef.9.15. Levit.11.38. Numer.19.20. & 24.7. & inde non sequitur מַיִם esse singulare, scribit Aben Esra, ad locum priorem. Sæpe enim verbum singulare cum Nomine plurali jungitur per synthesin. Constr. מֵי; Genef.7.7. Et servato utroque Mem, מֵימֵי; Exod.7.19. & sic semper cum Affixis מֵימֶיךָ Aquas tuas, Num.26.19.
מִין m. Species: Aff. לְמִינוֹ Secundum speciem suam, Gen.1.11. לְמִינֵהוּ In species suas, v.12.
מֵיץ m. Pressura: מֵיץ חָלָב pressura lactis, וּמֵיץ אַף Et pressura nasi, מֵיץ אַפַּיִם Et pressura irarum, Prov.30.33.
מֵץ m. Pressor: אַפֵּס הַמֵּץ Definet[?] qui premat, Jes.16.4.
מָכַךְ Depauperari, Attenuari. Futur. וַיִּמְּכוּ Et attenuati fuerunt, Psalm.106.43. quâ significatione convenit cum מוּךְ. Niph. Futurum, יִמָּךְ[?]

page.notes: Running head and page number are printed at the top. The catchword "Attenua-" is printed at lower right. The Hebrew vocalisation and some Hebrew forms in the entries (for example in the Niph. Futurum line of מָכַךְ, and the Hebrew of the first continuation line) are hard to read at this resolution and are marked [?] where doubtful. "Definet" is read from the scan and may be "Desinet". Faint digitiser text at the bottom right is not transcribed.
